messages.author: 26c971075f8aedcc
messages.subject: RAM usage on large models
parts:
Hi,

I am running INLA on some large models (~80K observations with a latent field of ~110K nodes). I experienced repeated crashes fitting these models. After inspecting the verbose output I did not notice anything meaningful. However, checking the amount of resources used (CPU and RAM) I noticed very large RAM consumption at the end of run (~30 GB), while it was less than 5GB (using 4 threads via num.threads) or less than 2GB (using 1 thread via num.threads) most of job run - see the attached figures (blue is INLA). Is this amount of RAM usage expected for such a kind of a model and data? Is there any way to reduce it, by fitting more coarse approximations?

Thanks!

Regards, Gregor

messages.author: 26c971075f8aedcc
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] RAM usage on large models
parts:
Hi,

I have tried using num.threads and it did not had any sizeable effect on RAM usage, bit it did have expected effect for the CPU usage as shown on plots in previous e-mail.

I have tried now using the EB integration strategy and this cuts down RAM usage by 10x - see attached plots in this e-mail. This gives me now quite some space to go ahead.

gg


On 19 January 2014 20:08, Finn Lindgren <finn.l...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi,
Yes, the integration part uses memory for each thread; compare with setting num.threads=1.
The optimization part isn't as parallel.

Inla uses a lot less memory for big models nowadays than a few years ago, but still a lot more than it really needs to use; redesign/implementation likely needed to fix it...

Finn
